parameters.content:
## What this is

Error handler for the `Certificate Renewal Reminders` workflow. Set it as that workflow's Error Workflow (Workflow Settings > Error Workflow).

Keep it **published**. Some n8n instances refuse an unpublished workflow as an error workflow, and only say so when you try to attach it.

## What it does

When a scheduled run fails outright, this records the failure in the failures Data Table: when it happened, which workflow and node, the error message and a link to the execution.

Failures are reviewed in that table. There is deliberately no alert. Add an email or chat node after `Record Failure` once you have agreed a sending route.

## Why it does not write to Administrate

The main workflow logs to Administrate through `externalLog.createExternalIntegrationLog`. This deliberately does not.

`nodeId` on that mutation is `ID!` and anchors the entry to a record. The error trigger payload carries workflow and execution metadata only, never the failing run's own data, so no event ID is available here. For the most likely failures, a configuration guard refusing or a register read failing, no event has even been identified yet, so there is nothing to anchor an entry to.

Handled per-event failures still log to Administrate from inside the main workflow, where the event ID is in hand.

## Testing it

An error workflow fires on production executions only, never on manual ones, so a manual run of the main workflow will not reach this however it fails. To test it, publish a throwaway workflow that throws deliberately, set this as its Error Workflow and confirm a row appears.

## The execution link

`execution.url` on the trigger payload can resolve to `http://localhost:5678` when no editor base URL is configured. The link is therefore built from `instanceBase_str` in `Shape Failure Row`. Set it to your n8n host.
